text:
marco: quick postmortem summary — tenant X had multiple model fallbacks this morning due to pin churn. looks like version pinning + our rollout metadata semantics aren't expressive enough for in-flight renewals.
sylvie: can you sketch the failure chain? was it TTL-only or something more subtle?
marco: TTL-only + optimistic client heuristics. client saw a recent update and kept serving, control plane batched commit and GC assumed expiry. result: evictions -> slower variant -> 5xx spike for a subset of requests.
arun: we've debated soft/hard TTLs before. wondering if we can add an explicit "commit_guarantee" signal instead of only time-based heuristics. that way clients know when a renewal is durable vs provisional.
sylvie: that aligns with ops request for provenance. my take: add a compact metadata block to rollout pin: fields: lease_seq (int), commit_ts_ms, grace_ms, commit_state enum {provisional, durable}, and optional commit_sig (opaque). clients use commit_state + lease_seq to validate caches.
marco: tradeoffs?
arun: commit_sig gives stronger guarantees (signed/opaque) but needs key management. commit_state alone is weaker but simpler. grace_ms lets us control short-term allowances for provisional commits.
sylvie: propose a combined minimal schema so we can iterate: lease_seq (ms-int as string), commit_ts_ms (string), commit_state (string), grace_ms (string), origin_tags (list-ish string). example in docs:
```json
{"lease_seq":"1234","commit_ts_ms":"1712345678000","commit_state":"provisional","grace_ms":"3000","origin_tags":"autoscaler,canary"}
```
marco: naming note: prefer "commit_state" over "renewal_hint" to avoid overloaded renewal language. also keep TTLs normalized to ms on the wire.
arun: client policy suggestion: when commit_state=="provisional", only allow cached pin if now < commit_ts_ms + grace_ms AND cached_lease_seq == lease_seq. otherwise re-resolve. this avoids relying solely on soft_ttl semantics.
sylvie: we need metrics: provisional_use_count, provisional_expire_misses, lease_seq_mismatch_rate. plus an alert if provisional->durable transitions lag > 5s.
marco: security: commit_sig must be HMAC with per-cluster key; don't put any secret plaintext. also rotate keys and emit key_id in metadata if present.
arun: backwards compat: servers may not emit new fields. clients must default commit_state to "durable" and grace_ms to 0 to avoid unnecessary churn for older tenants.
sylvie: testing: 1) simulated batching delays with 0-5s commit lag; 2) client time-skew scenarios (+/- 2s); 3) canary overrides where emit state flips quickly. include chaos test that injects GC at commit boundaries.
marco: rollout plan: stage 1 — control plane emits metadata read-only for 2 weeks (clients ignore). stage 2 — release client libs that optionally honor commit_state behind feature flag. stage 3 — enable GC to consult commit_state with feature flag turned on for a small cohort. monitor metrics & rollback path.
arun: API shape discussion: should we put the block at top-level pin object or inside a 'lease_metadata' subfield? top-level is easier for small clients, but nested keeps future fields tidy.
sylvie: prefer 'lease_metadata' to avoid polluting main pin surface; but ensure lightweight clients can still parse without heavy deps. represent origin_tags as comma-separated string to keep schema flat for now.
marco: example canonical payload (ms ints, flat values):
lease_seq: "1234"
commit_ts_ms: "1712345678000"
commit_state: "provisional"
grace_ms: "3000"
origin_tags: "autoscaler,canary-7"
commit_sig: "k1:hb3..."
key_id: "k1"
arun: operational acceptance criteria: no increase in eviction rate post-rollout, provisional_mismatch_metric < threshold, dashboards for provisional transition latency.
sylvie: client library guidance: parse ms ints, expose a helper isPinValid(cached_metadata, server_metadata, now_ms) that prefers re-resolve on mismatch. ship implementations in SDKs (go, python, node) before flipping GC behavior.
marco: PRs: i'll open RFC with exact schema + migration notes. can we also include an optional 'compat_level' integer so we can evolve semantics without breaking older clients? start with compat_level=1.
arun: good idea. clients can check compat_level and opt into advanced semantics when >=2.
sylvie: release-bot: canary window request queued for branch 'lease-compact-state' — tentative 2026-04-10 01:00 UTC for 5%.
release-bot: canary scheduled (id: canary-3401).
marco: thanks team. @sylvie can you draft the SDK helper signatures and tests? i'll add the RFC and ops checklist.
sylvie: on it. short follow-up PR in the morning.
ops-bot: INF-4789 opened to track key rotation and telemetry dashboards.
marco: perfect. closing notes: try to keep metadata compact (no large blobs) and favor ms-int values for telemetry consistency. we'll reconvene after RFC review.
